p_body: There exists a language older than words, spoken not through the tongue but through textures, colours, rhythms and silences. It is the language of nature — a soft, persistent whisper that surrounds us, though few have the patience to listen. In the rustling of leaves, the migration of birds, the bloom of a lone flower amidst a barren field, nature offers a narrative both timeless and ever-changing. At dawn, the sky does not shout but blushes in subtle hues of amber and rose, as though shy to announce the new day. Trees sway not with urgency but with quiet grace, teaching that strength and stillness are not opposing forces. The river, unhurried, carries through mountains and meadows alike, murmuring ancient truths about perseverance and purpose. Even the decay of autumn, so often associated with death, carries within it the promise of renewal, of a spring yet to come. Yet, in our rush to modernize, we have dulled our senses to these subtle signs. We measure success in speed and numbers, often forgetting that not all value can be calculated. Technology may have extended our reach, but it has also narrowed our gaze. ---

p_body: Technological advancement has undeniably transformed human life, often for the better. Innovations in medicine, communications and transportation have expanded horizons and improved living standards. Yet, there remains an underlying paradox: as societies become more technologically advanced, individuals often report feeling more disconnected, anxious and overwhelmed. This contradiction is not merely anecdotal. Numerous studies suggest a correlation between digital dependency and declining mental well-being. The convenience of instant communication, for instance, has paradoxically eroded the depth of interpersonal relationships. Similarly, the promise of efficiency brought by automation and artificial intelligence has, in some sectors, resulted in job displacement and a growing sense of purposelessness. Moreover, the constant pursuit of progress has fostered a culture of perpetual urgency. The pressure to stay updated, to be productive and to remain relevant has blurred the boundaries between personal and professional lives. Instead of liberating individuals, modern technologies often act as invisible shackles, tethering them to devices and schedules. ---
q_hi: What is the central paradox discussed in the passage?

b_hi: Innovation always leads to job creation.
